name: Confidence Rating (Metacognitive)
summary: After answering a question, learners rate their confidence (low/med/high); scoring multiplies by confidence level.

aiGenerability.notes: Pure mechanic overlay. No additional content generation beyond any base question's content. Works with any other mechanic: multiple choice, true-false, open-ended, etc. Zero AI complexity.

baseQuestionId.description: Reference to any base mechanic's content (e.g., a multiple-choice question). This mechanic overlays confidence rating on top.

confidenceLevels.description: The confidence options. Ages 8-10: ['Not sure', 'Pretty sure']. Ages 11-16: ['Low', 'Medium', 'High']. Can use emoji for young learners.

scoringMultiplier.description: Multiplier for each confidence level. e.g., {'Low': 1.0, 'Medium': 1.5, 'High': 2.0}. Correct answer + high confidence = max points. Wrong answer + high confidence = learning moment.

ux.mobileNotes: Appears below or beside the answer selection. For young learners, use emoji (😊 sure, 😕 not sure). Tap to select confidence level; immediate visual feedback (scaling, color change). Keep options horizontally arranged for quick scanning. Ensure adequate spacing between options to prevent mis-taps.

ageAdaptations.8-10: Two emoji-based confidence levels: 😊 Sure / 😕 Not Sure. Large, tappable emoji buttons. Multiplier: Sure = 2x, Not Sure = 1x. Celebratory feedback when learner is correct + confident, encouraging feedback when wrong + not confident.
ageAdaptations.11-13: Three text-based levels: Low, Medium, High. Multiplier: Low = 1x, Medium = 1.5x, High = 2x. Feedback includes reflection: 'You got it right and were confident! Great job.' or 'You weren't sure and that was wise given the difficulty.'
ageAdaptations.14-16: Three levels with detailed feedback on calibration: 'Your confidence matches your accuracy. Keep it up!' or 'You were overconfident on this question. How can you improve?' Learner sees a calibration graph over multiple questions (confidence vs. accuracy) to track metacognitive growth.
